tasks.summary: The diff makes `handleTrackerSync` accept an omitted `epicHash` and refresh every Epic through a new `syncRepository` wrapper with a per-repository in-flight guard (`refreshing` Set), while leaving the single-Epic path byte-for-byte unchanged except the error message for an explicitly empty `epicHash`. The new test exercises the all-synced repo-wide path, the concurrent-call skip, post-completion re-run, and the unchanged single-Epic path; it passes, and the project typechecks clean. The implementation matches the LLD contract and the task's three acceptance checks exactly.

testCoverage.explanation: Inspected both committed blocks (test file and tracker-setup-handlers.ts) in full at commit 62e30ff0, plus the prior version at parent 52c23f14 to isolate the actual diff. The added test (`tracker.sync without an epicHash refreshes every Epic once, a second call while one runs is skipped, and a call with an epicHash is unchanged`) covers: (1) all-Epics-synced repo-wide call returning `{status:'synced', refreshed:2}` with exactly 4 issue reads (an Epic+Story pair per of 2 Epics); (2) a concurrent second repo-wide call via `Promise.all` returning `{status:'skipped', reason:'a refresh of this repository is already running'}` while reading no additional issues — verified this is deterministic (not flaky) because `refreshing.add(repoPath)` executes synchronously before any awaited I/O in `syncRepository`/`refreshTrackerStatus`/`syncTracker`, so the second array element of `Promise.all` always observes the guard set; (3) a normal run after the first ends; (4) the single-Epic path (`epicHash: HASH2`) returning the unchanged `SyncResult` shape. Ran the test file directly (`npx tsx --test-force-exit src/daemon/__tests__/tracker-sync-method.test.ts`) — both the new and the pre-existing test in that file pass, including the new empty-string-epicHash error case. Ran `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` — clean. The `syncRepository` wrapper's own `failed`/`skipped`-summarization branches (as opposed to the `synced` branch, which is exercised) are not directly exercised by a test at this level, but they only re-map fields (`status`, joined `warnings`) that are already behaviorally proven in the pre-existing, unmodified `src/workflow/tracker/__tests__/refresh.test.ts` (failed reads, skipped-with-reason, warnings array) — and the LLD's own acceptanceMapping (ac4) names only this one test for the repo-wide refresh, so the test scope matches the design's own strategy rather than an omission introduced by this task.

The documentation's claims were checked against the actual code: repository-wide tracker.sync and its per-repo in-flight guard (tracker-setup-handlers.ts), the gitHooks setting semantics and partial-install behavior (git-hooks-methods.ts apply()), uninstall's delete-if-empty behavior and status's foreign/earlyExit/stale reporting (hook-block.ts / hook-inspect.ts), the git-path resolution via `git rev-parse --git-path hooks` (defaultHooksDir), the repo-call-audit 'modifying' classification of tracker.sync/repo.gitHooks.* (the worktree-refusal claim), and the isolated-read core.hooksPath=/dev/null mechanism — all matched. All three of t7's PLAN acceptance checks are met: the real-git test (checked here), the documentation content (checked here), and the sweep-suite comparison, which is recorded in docs/standalone/.../S001/SWEEP.md (committed in a separate same-day commit for this task, not part of the diff under review but present in the current tree as corroborating evidence) and whose findings I independently reproduced by rerunning git-hooks-methods.test.ts and the new test itself.
